= Glasgow Research: Complete Free-Space Directory =

This is the navigation directory for the Glasgow Name Study. Each substantive page covers a distinct person, place, record group, branch or hypothesis. Alternative titles route readers to the relevant central page.

{| class="wikitable" style="background:#f8fff8; width:100%;"
! Page type
! Meaning
! Reader action
|-
| '''Project hub'''
| current synthesis or primary route through the study
| begin here
|-
| '''Evidence hub'''
| sourced register or branch study with an explicit current conclusion
| use for established findings and evidence limits
|-
| '''Specialist study'''
| focused person, place, family, source set or research question
| check its evidence statement before reusing a claim
|-
| '''Record notebook'''
| transcription, extract or working collection awaiting full resolution
| cite the underlying record, not the notebook alone
|-
| '''Hypothesis / notebook'''
| research leads preserved for testing; not a documented project conclusion
| follow its link to the relevant evidence hub
|}

'''Recommended route:''' read the [[Space:Glasgow Name Study#current_conclusion|project conclusion]], choose the relevant evidence hub below, then use the specialist pages for the underlying detail. The [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/catalogue Research Catalogue], [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/records/ Record Search], [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/places/ Place Search] and [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/map/ Family Map] provide faster discovery across the corpus. They are finding aids; facts still require the cited historical record.

! Research page !! Evidence-bearing material !! Hypotheses requiring support !! Next action

|-
| [[Space:Glasgow Origins Research (1170 - 1600)|Origins Research, 1170–1600]] || bearer list and source leads route to the chronological register || a single nested medieval-to-modern pedigree || check each unabsorbed reference independently
|-
| [[Space:Glasgow Kinship Circle|Kinship Circle]] || repeated marriage and witness-network questions route to the specialist marriage study || network proximity as proof of parentage or identity || test each proposed edge with a relationship-bearing record
|-
| [[Space:Glasgow Surname Protocol Books|Protocol Books]] || relationship-bearing entries now have a structured index || raw OCR or notebook wording as a final citation || complete the missing volume, page and protocol-number citations
|-
| [[Space:Glasgow Wills & Testaments|Wills and Testaments]] || household groups now have a structured index and explicit evidence status || same-name identifications without the testament text || obtain stable catalogue links or images and transcribe relationship clauses
|-
| [[Space:Glasgow Ancient YDNA|Ancient Y-DNA]] || current topology, platform resources and evidential limits || named medieval SNP assignments unsupported by a pedigree or ancient sample || update only from current platform results and supported comparisons
|-
| [[Space:Personal genetic exploration|Personal genetic exploration]] || retained as a transparent personal notebook || private match observations as project conclusions || transfer only anonymised, reproducible conclusions with consent
|-
| [[Space:Other Medevil Glasgow Candidates|Other medieval candidates]] || useful controls and possible exclusions || candidates treated as Glasgow bearers merely because of proximity || correct the title by controlled move and continue source-by-source exclusions
|}

== Contribute and report corrections ==

Anyone may improve WikiTree's Glasgow profiles and free-space pages. Add a citation to the underlying record, distinguish transcription from interpretation, and label a proposed identity or relationship as a hypothesis. Project-wide data corrections may also be reported through the [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/feedback workbench feedback page].

New specialist pages should be linked here and from the nearest evidence hub. New pre-1500 people must be represented by an individual free-space page and added in chronological order to the pre-1500 register; do not create a pre-1500 WikiTree person profile for this study.

== Houses ==
The surnames'' "Clerk", "Grahame", "Spruell", and "Anderson"'' are mentioned frequently alongside the first apperance of the Glasgows in the Protocol books (16C)

<blockquote>2916. Angus— Darroch, spouses. 1 September, 1586, 9 a.m. 
George Glasgw, son and heir of William Glasgow, with consent of 
Margaret Herbesoun, his mother, for her liferent, and of Sir William 
Herbesoun and Stephen Glasgw, his curators, sold to John Angus, merchant 
in Glasgow, and Helen Darrocht, spouses, a back waste ruinous tenement^ with 
the pertinents, lying on the west side of the street leading from the metropolitan 
church to the market cross, between the lands sometime of Robert Pirrhie, 
then of John Clerk, tailor, on the east, the lands of q. David Lyndsay on 
the west, the lands of Sir Bartholomew Sympsoun on the north, and the 
lands of q. George Herbesoun on the south. Sasine given by John Grahame, 
bailie. Witnesses: John Clerk, tailor, citizen, and John Pirrhie, writer.
</blockquote>
